part_1:
Udom: Hello everyone. Today's weather is really nice — perfect for the Bun Bang Fai festival.

Somphon: Yes, Chief Udom. More people have come this year than last year.

Nittaya: I'm so excited. I haven't attended this event since last year. I really missed this atmosphere.

Amphon: Yes, Nittaya. I also missed the loud rockets and the fun folk performances.

Udom: This year we have new performances too — both molam and performances from the village children.

Somphon: The kids have been rehearsing a lot. I hope everyone likes it.

Nittaya: I'm sure it'll be fun. The children are all talented.

Amphon: Chief Udom, is there anything in particular you'd recommend we see?

Udom: If possible, I'd like everyone to watch the rocket contest. This year teams from nearby villages are joining.

Somphon: Oh, that's interesting. I'll take my friends to see it for sure.

Nittaya: Great. I want to see how beautiful each team's rockets are.

Amphon: Let's go then, so we don't miss anything fun.

Udom: Let's go, everyone. I hope you all enjoy today's festival.
part_2:
Somphon: Sorry everyone, I have to pick up some medicine first. I'll be back.

Amphon: I have to grab some snacks first too. See you later.

Udom: Okay, Somphon, Amphon, see you later.

Nittaya: Chief Udom, I've noticed Somphon looks stressed lately.

Udom: Yes, Nittaya. I noticed it too. He doesn't seem as cheerful as before.

Nittaya: Is he having some problem?

Udom: He told me he feels pressured by life in the village. Sometimes it may be because of the many responsibilities he has.

Nittaya: I understand. Sometimes staying in the same place for a long time can make someone feel bored.

Udom: Yes. I try to let him rest, but I don't know how much that helps.

Nittaya: If there's anything I can do to help, tell me. Sometimes talking with a friend can make him feel better.

Udom: Thank you, Nittaya. I'll try talking to him again.

Nittaya: I hope he feels better soon.

Udom: Yes, I hope so too. Thanks for caring about Somphon.
part_3:
Amphon: I'm back. Sorry for being gone so long.

Udom: Welcome back, Amphon. We were just talking about weather forecasts for agriculture.

Amphon: Oh good. I'm interested in that too. How's the weather lately?

Nittaya: They said rain will decrease during this period, but there is still a chance of rain in some areas.

Udom: Yes, but we must also watch for flooding in areas that get heavy rain.

Amphon: That's true. If it rains less, farmers must prepare to deal with water shortages.

Nittaya: Yes, planning water use appropriately is very important.

Udom: Do you have any agricultural advice, Amphon?

Amphon: I think using technology to assist agriculture would be very beneficial, like using weather forecast apps.

Udom: I agree. Technology helps us plan better.

Amphon: Yes, but I have to go out to take care of a small errand now. See you again.

Nittaya: Good luck, Amphon. See you.

Udom: Take care, Amphon. See you.

Amphon: Thanks everyone. Goodbye.
part_4:
Somphon: I'm back everyone. Sorry I was gone so long.

Udom: Welcome back, Somphon.

Nittaya: Glad you're back, Somphon.

Somphon: Thank you. I have a question about the weather forecast. Chief Udom, do you know if the rain will be good this year?

Udom: This year it will definitely rain. The rice will sprout and prosper for sure.

Nittaya: Yes, Somphon. Don't worry. This should be a good year for farmers.

Somphon: Thank you very much. Hearing that gives me a lot of encouragement.

Udom: I'm glad to hear that. If there's anything we can help with, tell us.

Nittaya: Yes, we're always ready to help.

Somphon: Thank you all very much. I feel much better.

Sawat: Yes, Prasoet. Anything new this year? I heard there's a traditional performance.

Prasoet: Yes, this year there's a nang talung (traditional shadow puppet) show. It's very interesting.

Somchit: Oh, that's great. I love nang talung. When I was a child my grandmother often took me to see it.

Somsak: Yes, Somchit, I remember when we were kids we used to go watch together. It was so much fun.

Sawat: Shall we go watch it together this year? I think it's a good chance to spend time together.

Prasoet: Of course. We should go together so we can make good memories again.

Somchit: I agree. After that, shall we have dinner together?

Somsak: Sounds great. I know a very tasty Southern restaurant nearby.

Sawat: Then it's settled: we'll watch the nang talung and then have dinner together.

part_1:
Narong: It's really busy today; the Hat Yai fried chicken shop is completely full.

Udom: Yes. During Loy Krathong people often go out to eat.

Thawi: Is there anything special anyone wants to eat? I saw they have a new menu item.

Somphon: I'd like to try the new fried chicken recipe they advertised. It looks delicious.

Narong: Then shall we order the new fried chicken first, and also get extra sticky rice?

Udom: Sounds good. And don't forget to order the special dipping sauce — I really like it.

Thawi: Sure. I'll go order the food. Does anyone want anything to drink?

Somphon: I'll have a soda.

Narong: I'll just have water.

Udom: I'll have coconut water; it's refreshing.

Thawi: Okay, I'll be back shortly with the food.

Narong: Thank you, Mom.

Somphon: Thank you, sister.

Udom: Thanks, dear.

Thawi: It's okay. I'll be back with delicious food soon.
part_2:
Udom: Sorry everyone, I need to go grab some snacks or drinks. I'll be right back.

Somphon: I need to go charge my laptop first. I'll be back.

Narong: Okay, see you in a bit.

Thawi: See you soon.

Narong: Thawi, I feel like Udom seems stressed lately.

Narong: I think he might feel like he hasn't given enough attention to certain things.

Thawi: Right. Maybe he feels like he hasn't been spending much time with us.

Narong: I think if we talk to him together, it might make him feel better.

Thawi: I agree. Sometimes just letting him know we're by his side can help.

Narong: Yes. We should encourage him more.

Thawi: Let's talk to him when he returns.

Narong: Good. Thank you, Thawi, for understanding and helping think of ideas.

Thawi: It's nothing. We're family; we should always help each other.
part_3:

Narong: My older brother said work has been very busy lately, but he's holding up.

Thawi: My sister said that after the crisis her sales haven't been good, but she's doing her best.

Somphon: I understand. Many people are facing the same problems these days.

Narong: Yes, but we have to keep fighting.

Thawi: Right, we need to encourage each other.

Somphon: I have to quickly tidy up the room before my next meeting. See you later.

Narong: Okay, Somphon. See you.

Thawi: Good luck, Somphon.

Wichian: It's okay, Sombat. See you next time.

Somphon: Yes, don't worry.

Sawat: I have to go take care of my child for a moment. See you later.

Wichian: Okay, Sawat. Take good care of your child.

Somphon: Yes. Now it's just the two of us left, Wichai.

Wichian: That's right. I think Sombat must be worried about work.

Somphon: Yes. He seems like someone who takes his responsibilities seriously.

Wichian: Right. He always pays attention to every detail.

Somphon: I hope he can handle everything smoothly.

Wichian: I hope so too. What should we do next?

Somphon: Shall we take a walk around the temple? The atmosphere is really nice.

Wichian: Sounds good, let's go.

Sawat: Hello everyone, I'm back.

Wichian: Welcome back, Sawat! How's your child?

Sawat: My child is fine, thanks for asking. What have you all been doing?

Somphon: We've been walking around the temple. The atmosphere is wonderful.

Sawat: That's great. I really miss this kind of atmosphere in my hometown.

Wichian: Yes, returning to your hometown for Songkran is really special.

Somphon: Yes, you get to see family and eat the food you miss.

Sawat: Exactly. Sometimes I skip meals and lose sleep to prepare to go home.

Wichian: That's true. Sometimes preparing to go home is exhausting.

Somphon: But once you meet your family, you forget about the tiredness.

Sawat: Yes, but I have to go now — unexpected guests have arrived.

Wichian: Okay, Sawat, see you again.

Somphon: Yes, take care.

Sawat: Thank you, everyone. Goodbye.

Sombat: Hello everyone, I'm back.

Wichian: Welcome back, Sombat!

Somphon: Yes, glad to see you again.

Sombat: Thank you. But I noticed Wichai looks tired — is something wrong?

Wichian: Oh, it's nothing. Just not getting enough rest.

Somphon: Yes, the work isn't difficult; it's nothing serious.

Sombat: That's good. Don't forget to take care of your health.

Wichian: Thank you, Sombat. I'll try to rest more.

Somphon: Yes, rest a lot so you have energy to keep working.

Sombat: Good. If there's anything I can help with, let me know.

Wichian: Thank you, Sombat.

Somphon: Yes, thank you very much.

part_1:
Narong: Hello everyone. What do we need to do today at Dong Suea Ten Monastery?

Chan: Hello, Venerable Narong. I'm here to help clean the temple. Is there anything else you'd like me to help with?

Nittaya: Hello, Khun Chan. Today we'll clean the assembly hall and prepare the place for tomorrow's merit-making ceremony.

Somchit: Yes. We expect many people at tomorrow's ceremony, so we need to get everything ready.

Narong: Great. Thank you, Chan, for coming to help. Shall we start by sweeping the temple courtyard?

Chan: Sure, Venerable Narong. I'll go get a broom.

Nittaya: I'll help arrange flowers in the hall so it looks nice to welcome everyone.

Somchit: I'll take care of the drinking water and snacks for tomorrow so we don't run short.

Narong: Thank you all very much for your help. Tomorrow's merit-making will certainly go well.

Chan: It's nothing, Venerable. This is a good opportunity for me to make merit and help the temple.

Nittaya: Yes. Helping out like this feels very good.

Somchit: Right. Making merit together makes us feel part of the community.

Narong: I rejoice in your merit, everyone. May you all be happy and prosper in the Dhamma.
part_2:
Chan: Sorry everyone, I have to go attend to someone who just arrived. See you later.

Somchit: I also have to go check on an urgent matter. Sorry.

Narong: It's all right, Chan, Somchit. Thank you for coming to help.

Nittaya: Thank you very much. See you again.

(Chan and Somchit leave the conversation)

Narong: Nittaya, I'm a bit worried about Chan. He seems to have something on his mind.

Nittaya: Yes, I noticed too. He looks sad; he might have personal problems.

Narong: I think we should talk with him more, in case we can help.

Nittaya: I agree. Sometimes talking can make him feel better.

Narong: Yes. Having friends who are willing to listen is important.

Nittaya: If he needs help, we're ready to stand by him.

Narong: Of course. We'll do our best to take care of our friend.
part_3:
Somchit: I'm back. Sorry I had to leave in a hurry earlier.

Narong: It's okay, Somchit. You returned just in time.

Nittaya: Glad you're back, Somchit. We were talking about making offerings and praying for forgiveness after wrongdoing.

Somchit: Hmm, interesting. I think making offerings is a good deed, but sometimes merit alone isn't enough; effort is also needed.

Narong: I agree. Doing good is valuable, but we must try to improve ourselves as well.

Nittaya: Yes. Praying is also a way to set goals for ourselves.

Somchit: Right. Determination to do good and trying our best is important.

Narong: Yes. Putting in effort helps us achieve what we intend.

Somchit: Sorry, I just remembered I have to handle some paperwork. Excuse me.

Nittaya: It's fine, Somchit. Thank you for joining the discussion.

Narong: Thank you, Somchit. See you again.

Somchit: Thank you everyone. Goodbye.

(Somchit leaves the conversation)
part_4:
Chan: Hello everyone, I'm back. Sorry I had to rush off earlier.

Narong: Welcome back, Chan. Can we help you with anything?

Chan: Thank you, Venerable. Actually I have something I'd like to consult about.

Nittaya: Sure, Chan. How can we help?

Chan: I wonder whether the merit we make can wash away the wrongs we've done?

Narong: The merit we make can help us feel better and support us in improving ourselves.

Nittaya: Yes. Making merit brings happiness and inner peace, which gives us the strength and will to correct our mistakes.

Chan: Thank you very much. I feel much better.

Narong: You're welcome, Chan. Having the intention to improve yourself is a good thing.

Nittaya: Yes. Your intention shows you're heading in the right direction.

Chan: Thank you. I'll try to do my best.

part_1:
Wichian: Hello, layman Udom. Do you have any business at Dong Suea Ten Monastery today?

Udom: Hello, Venerable Wichian. I'm just here to make merit and listen to Dhamma today.

Thawi: It's good that you come often, Udom. Listening to the Dhamma helps calm the mind.

Udom: Yes, Venerable Thawi. I feel that every time I come here I always learn something new.

Wichai: Udom, do you have any questions about the Dhamma you'd like to ask?

Udom: Yes, Venerable Wichai. I wonder why meditation is so important in daily life.

Wichian: Meditation helps us be mindful and aware in every moment, enabling us to handle problems better.

Thawi: That's right. Practicing meditation trains the mind to be strong and steady.

Udom: Thank you, Venerable. I'll try to practice meditation more.

Wichai: Very good, Udom. If you have any further questions, feel free to ask.

Udom: Thank you all, Venerables. I'm glad to be here.
part_2:
Udom: Sorry, Venerable. I have to check something first. See you later.

Wichai: No problem, Udom. See you later. Good luck.

Udom: Thank you all, Venerables. Goodbye.

Wichai: I must take my leave as well—there's an urgent matter to attend to.

Wichian: Understood, Venerable Wichai. Goodbye.

Thawi: Goodbye, Venerable Wichai.

(After Udom and Wichai leave)

Wichian: Udom seems to have worries.

Thawi: Yes, I noticed he looked sad.

Wichian: Perhaps he feels discouraged about something in life.

Thawi: We should find a way to help encourage him.

Wichian: Yes. Support from those around him is very important.

Thawi: If he has another chance to talk with us, we should give good advice.

Wichian: Agreed. Sometimes just listening attentively helps a lot.

Thawi: I hope Udom gets through this period well.

Wichian: Yes. We will always stand by him.
part_3:
Wichai: I'm back. Sorry I had to leave earlier.

Wichian: Welcome back, Venerable Wichai.

Thawi: Glad you're back, Venerable.

Wichai: Thank you. So, what were you talking about?

Wichian: We were discussing offering alms and praying for blessings after wrongdoing.

Thawi: Yes. Offering alms is a way to show remorse and pray for a better life.

Wichai: Making merit is good, but merit alone is not enough; effort is also necessary.

Somsak: Exactly, Udom. Don't forget we're always by your side.

Udom: Thank you all so much. You really make me feel a lot better.

Sawat: How are you holding up, Udom? Are you managing okay?

Udom: I'm trying. I still feel sad sometimes, but I have to keep going.

Prasoet: If you want to rest or get a change of scenery, tell us. We'll take you out.

Somsak: Yeah, a trip would be good — help you relax a bit.

Udom: Thanks a lot. I'll let you know when I'm ready.

Somsak: That's right. We're here for you.

Udom: Thanks again, you guys are the best friends anyone could ask for.

Thawi: Hello everyone. What do we need to do today?

Somchai: Hello Thawi. Today we need to check the orderliness in Zone C.

Amphon: Yes, and we also need to prepare the documents for tomorrow's family visits.

Samran: Hello officers. May I ask what time my family can visit tomorrow?

Thawi: Hello Samran. Family visits are allowed from 9 AM to 3 PM tomorrow.

Samran: Thank you very much. I'll tell my family.

Somchai: Samran, how are you these days? Is there anything you'd like us to help with?

Samran: I'm okay. Thanks for asking. If anything comes up, I'll let you know.

Amphon: That's good. If you have any problems, don't forget to tell us.

Thawi: Right. We're always ready to help. Alright, let's get back to work.

Somchai: Let's go, or we'll be late.

Amphon: Okay, let's go.

Samran: Thank you, officers.
part_2:

Amphon: I need to go pick up the snacks first. I'll be back later.

Thawi: Okay Samran, Amphon — see you later.

Somchai: Travel safely.

(Samran and Amphon leave the conversation)

Thawi: Somchai, what do you think we should do about Samran?

Somchai: I've been thinking. Maybe he needs someone to talk to more often.

Thawi: Yes, I feel he might be a bit discouraged.

Somchai: We should try inviting him for talks regularly, let him know we're ready to help.

Thawi: I agree. Sometimes talking can help him feel better.

Somchai: Right. Sometimes just having someone listen helps a lot.

Thawi: Then let's schedule regular times to talk with him, okay?

Somchai: Good. I'll help take care of that.

Thawi: Thank you, Somchai. Let's work together to take the best care of Samran.

Somchai: Of course. We'll do our best.
part_3:
Amphon: I'm back. Sorry for being gone so long.

Thawi: Welcome back, Amphon. Is there anything else we need to do?

Amphon: Nothing further, but I think we should discuss reintegration into society.

Somchai: Yes, it's very important. Some people may find it hard to make a living in a struggling economy.

Thawi: And it's even harder if they have a criminal record.

Amphon: That's true; finding a job is very challenging.

Somchai: Should we have support programs or training of some kind?

Thawi: That would be good — at least give them additional skills.

Amphon: I agree, but I need to stretch a little now. Excuse me.

Thawi: Okay, Amphon. See you later.

Somchai: Take care.

Amphon: Thanks. See you.

Amphon: Hello everyone. Today we're here to talk with you, Chan, about the incident that occurred.

Chan: Hello, officers. I'm ready to provide any information I know.

Somchai: Chan, could you tell us what happened on September 15?

Chan: Sure. That day I was at a friend's house in town, then someone called to tell me something happened at my shop.

Prasoet: What did you do after receiving the call?

Chan: I drove back to the shop immediately, but when I arrived there were police everywhere.

Amphon: Chan, did you speak with anyone at the shop that day?

Chan: I spoke with one of the employees. He said he saw a stranger come into the shop before the incident.

Somchai: Do you know that stranger?

Chan: No, I don't. But the employee said he was wearing a black shirt and had tattoos on his arm.

Prasoet: Thank you for the information, Chan. If there's anything else we'll contact you again.

Chan: Okay, thank you officers.

Amphon: Thank you, Chan, for cooperating. We'll work hard to find the truth.

Chan: Thank you. I hope to hear good news soon.

Somchai: Yes, thank you.

(Chan and Prasoet leave the conversation)

Somchai: I think we need to find more evidence about the stranger who came to the shop.

Amphon: Yes, but I feel like Chan doesn't really want us to make any arrests.

Somchai: I noticed that too. Maybe he doesn't want the situation to get more complicated.

Amphon: Maybe, but we have to do our duty.

Somchai: Right. We'll probably need to talk to the shop employee further to gather more information.

Amphon: Agreed. That way we'll have enough information to proceed.

Somchai: Okay, let's prepare a plan.

Amphon: Good. We'll be able to work more effectively.

Amphon: We think we should use methods that don't make him feel overly pressured.

Somchai: Yes. We may need to negotiate and build trust.

Prasoet: I agree. Building trust is very important.

Amphon: What are your thoughts, Prasoet?

Prasoet: I think we should let him know we want to help him more than arrest him.

Somchai: That's a good idea. If he feels we're on his side, he may surrender more easily.

Prasoet: Right. But I have to leave now — I need to pick up my dry cleaning.

Amphon: Okay. Thank you for joining the discussion.

Somchai: Thank you, Prasoet.

Prasoet: What did you do after receiving the call?

Chan: I drove back to the shop immediately, but when I arrived there were police everywhere.

Amphon: Chan, did you speak with anyone at the shop that day?

Chan: I spoke with one of the employees. He said he saw a stranger come into the shop before the incident.

Somchai: Do you know that stranger?

Chan: No, I don't. But the employee said he was wearing a black shirt and had tattoos on his arm.

Prasoet: Thank you for the information, Chan. If there's anything else we'll contact you again.

Chan: Okay, thank you officers.

Amphon: Thank you, Chan, for cooperating. We'll work hard to find the truth.

Chan: Thank you. I hope to hear good news soon.

Prasoet: I have to excuse myself as well — I just remembered I need to submit some documents. Sorry.

Amphon: That's all right. Thank you for coming to help.

Somchai: Yes, thank you.

Somchai: I think we need to find more evidence about the stranger who came to the shop.

Amphon: Yes, but I feel like Chan doesn't really want us to make any arrests.

Somchai: I noticed that too. Maybe he doesn't want the situation to get more complicated.

Amphon: Maybe, but we have to do our duty.

Somchai: Right. We'll probably need to talk to the shop employee further to gather more information.

Amphon: Agreed. That way we'll have enough information to proceed.

Somchai: Okay, let's prepare a plan.

Amphon: Good. We'll be able to work more effectively.

Somchai: Yes. We may need to negotiate and build trust.

Somchai: Thank you, Prasoet.

Prasoet: Thanks. See you again.

Amphon: Mr. Udom, we just need some more information. If you're innocent, we can help you.

Charoen: If you have nothing to hide, we'll help prove your innocence.

Udom: Okay, thank you very much for understanding me.

Amphon: Yes, we won't let anyone be punished unfairly.

Udom: Thank you. I feel much better after talking with you.

topic.scenario: Inside the Nong Bang house, Linthin subdistrict, Thong Pha Phum district, Kanchanaburi province, on the day of the ancestral spirit worship ceremony (maakha) at Grandma Tee Thepwan's house.
topic.situation_topic: Family gathering to perform the ancestral spirit worship ceremony
topic.situation: On the evening of the scheduled ancestral worship ceremony, Chan received a phone call from his youngest sister saying she could not attend. This contradicted the iron rule Somphon strictly adheres to—that all descendants must be present for the ceremony to begin—causing Chan great anxiety. If the ceremony were canceled, it could mean life-threatening danger to the elder family members according to beliefs about offending spirits. The situation grew even tenser when Somphon began asking about who was missing and insisted the ceremony would not proceed unless everyone was present.
topic.lie_objective: To reassure the elderly in the house so they won't worry.
topic.leave_reason_B: Need to fix a temporary internet problem.
topic.leave_reason_D_1: Need to check an urgent matter.
topic.leave_reason_D_2: Need to use the bathroom.

relationship: Somphon is the elder in Chan's family; other family members include Sombun and Sombat.
character_roles: Somphon เป็นผู้อาวุโสในครอบครัวของ Chan Sombun Sombat

lie.real_reason_c: Somphon would be hurt if family members didn't take this ritual seriously, as it's important for the household's well‑being.
lie.lie_c: Say that a friend came and that everyone attended the ceremony.

part_1:
Chan: The weather's nice today, Uncle Somphon. It's perfect for the ceremony.

Somphon: That's right, my child. Today is the day we remember our ancestors; we must do our best.

Sombun: I've prepared the offerings, Uncle Somphon—fruits, sweets, and incense and candles.

Sombat: I'll help set up the altar, P' Sombun. I want everything to look tidy.

Somphon: Very good, my grandchildren. With everyone helping like this, our ancestors would be proud.

Chan: Uncle Somphon, I'm curious—why do we honor the ancestral spirits today?

Somphon: Today our ancestors return to visit the house. It's a day to show gratitude and thank them for protecting us.

Sombun: What do we have to do, Uncle?

Somphon: We must light incense and candles, offer prayers, and tell good stories to our ancestors.

Sombat: I think it's a good tradition. It keeps us connected to our roots.

Chan: Yes. I feel warm inside every time we perform this ceremony.

Somphon: Good. Keeping this tradition is important. Don't forget to pass it on to future generations.

Sombun: Of course, Uncle. I'll teach my children the importance of today.

Sombat: Me too. I'll do my best.

topic.scenario: Inside the house of Nong Bang, Lin Thin Subdistrict, Thong Pha Phum District, Kanchanaburi Province, on the day of the ancestral spirit-veneration ceremony (maakà) at Grandma Ti Thepwun's house
topic.situation_topic: A family gathering to perform the ancestral veneration ceremony
topic.situation: On the evening of the scheduled ancestral veneration ceremony, Wichai received a phone call from his youngest sister saying she could not attend. This contradicted the iron rule that Udom strictly upheld — that all descendants must be present before the ceremony can begin — and it caused Wichai great worry. If the ceremony were canceled, it could mean life-threatening danger to the elders in the family according to the belief that the spirits would be offended. The situation grew more tense when Udom began questioning who was missing and insisted he would not perform the ceremony if anyone was absent.

topic.scenario: At the front of a house in a devout Mon village on Ban Sae Road, Phra Pradaeng District, Samut Prakan Province, on the day of the Mon funeral ceremony (Fe Sang).
topic.situation_topic: The Mon custom of leading the corpse to the temple.
topic.situation: Wichian's grandparents recently passed away of old age. The family is preparing the funeral according to tradition. Wichian told Charoen that he must lead the procession carrying the corpse from the house to the temple and must not look back at any point along the route. While walking across the rice field, Charoen heard a voice calling from behind and glanced back. When they reached the temple, Charoen asked Wichian in front of everyone about the correct way to handle it.

topic.scenario: In front of a house in a devout Mon village on Ban Sae Road, Phra Pradaeng District, Samut Prakan Province, on the day of a Mon funeral ceremony (Feh-sang).
topic.situation_topic: The Mon custom of leading a corpse to the temple for the funeral ceremony.
topic.situation: Nittaya's grandparents have just died of old age; the family is preparing a traditional funeral. Nittaya tells Udom that she must be the one to lead the funeral procession from the house to the temple and must not look back at any point along the route. While walking through the rice fields, Udom heard someone calling from behind and turned to look. When they reached the temple, Udom asked Nittaya in front of everyone about the proper way to handle it.
topic.leave_reason_B: Need to speak briefly with someone.
topic.leave_reason_D_1: Remembered there was something urgent to deal with.
topic.leave_reason_D_2: Need to take a phone call.

relationship: Udom is a relative of Nittaya Somphon Prasoet.
character_roles: Udom เป็นญาติกับ Nittaya Somphon Prasoet

lie.real_reason_c: Udom will feel guilty and afraid for breaking the ritual, believing it could lead to being haunted by ancestral spirits.
lie.lie_c: Say it's alright, nothing happened; I also heard the calling sound.
lie.truth_c: Udom's turning back should not have happened and it's believed that the ancestors will haunt him.

part_1:
Nittaya: (looking around) There are a lot of people here today, Udom.

Udom: Yes, Nittaya. The Mon feh-sang funeral is very important. Everyone comes together to pay their respects.

Somphon: (nodding) That's right. I remember coming with my parents every year when I was a child.

Prasoet: (smiling) Same here, Somphon. It's a chance to meet relatives we don't see often.

Nittaya: (smiling) Yes. It's a good opportunity to talk and remember those who have passed.

Udom: (looking at the house) This house is still the same as I remember it.

Somphon: (laughing) Yes, Udom. This house has always been the center of our family.

Prasoet: (smiling) So what will we do after this?

Nittaya: (thinking) After the ceremony, shall we go eat together? There's a good Mon restaurant nearby.

Udom: (nodding) That sounds good, Nittaya. I think everyone will be hungry.

Somphon: (smiling) I agree. Let's go together.

Prasoet: (smiling) Then it's settled. Let's eat together after the ceremony.

Nittaya: (smiling) Okay. Let's wait until the ceremony is over, then go.

Udom: (smiling) All right. See you all at the restaurant.
part_2:
Udom: (apologetic) Sorry everyone, I need to go speak briefly with someone.

Prasoet: (remembering) Oh, I just remembered I have something urgent to take care of. Excuse me.

Nittaya: (nodding) It's okay, Udom, Prasoet. See you at the restaurant.

Somphon: (smiling) Yes, see you.

(Udom and Prasoet leave the conversation)

Nittaya: (turning to Somphon) Udom worries too much sometimes.

Somphon: (nodding) Yes, I've noticed he seems stressed.

Nittaya: (smiling) He's probably afraid of doing something wrong and facing something bad.

Somphon: (soft laugh) Yes, sometimes he worries too much about things like that.

Nittaya: (smiling) But it's understandable; sometimes we need to be cautious.

Somphon: (nodding) Yes, but I don't think Udom needs to worry that much.

Nittaya: (smiling) I hope he'll feel better after this.

Somphon: (smiling) Yes, we'll help him relax.

Nittaya: (smiling) Good. Then see you at the restaurant.

Somphon: (smiling) All right, see you.
part_3:
Prasoet: (walking back) I'm back. Sorry for being away so long.

Nittaya: (smiling) It's okay, Prasoet. We were just talking about the Mon custom of leading a corpse to the temple for the ceremony.

Somphon: That's right. I think it's a very interesting custom.

Prasoet: (nodding) Yes. I've heard that when leading the corpse to the temple, you're not allowed to look back because it's believed the ancestors will haunt you.

Nittaya: (smiling) Yes, it's an old belief.

Somphon: (soft laugh) Udom must be really afraid of this.

Prasoet: (smiling) Yes, he's very cautious.

Nittaya: (smiling) But it's a good thing; at least it makes us careful.

Prasoet: (looking at his phone) Oh, sorry. I need to take a phone call. Excuse me.

Somphon: (nodding) It's fine. See you later.

Nittaya: (smiling) Okay, see you.

Prasoet: (smiling) All right, see you.
part_4:
Udom: (walking back) I'm back, everyone. Sorry I was away so long.

Nittaya: (smiling) It's okay, Udom.

Udom: (smiling) Thank you, Nittaya. Is there anything I can help with now?

Nittaya: (sighing) My grandparents just passed away. The family is preparing a traditional funeral.

Udom: (sad-faced) I'm sorry for your loss, Nittaya. Let me know if there's anything I can do.

Nittaya: Thank you, Udom. I have to be the one to lead the funeral procession from the house to the temple, and I'm not allowed to look back at all along the route.

Udom: (nodding) I understand. Is there anything in particular to be careful about?

Nittaya: (faint smile) Just don't look back.

Somphon: (nodding) Yes, it's a custom we must follow.

Udom: (recalling) While we were walking through the fields, I heard someone calling from behind, so I turned to look.

Nittaya: (smiling) It's okay, Udom. Nothing happened.

Somphon: (smiling) Yes, I heard a calling sound too.

Udom: (relieved) Thank you for saying that. I feel much better.

Nittaya: (smiling) Don't worry. Everything will go smoothly.

Somphon: (smiling) Yes, we'll work together to make everything go smoothly.

Udom: (smiling) Thank you, everyone. I feel much better.

Prani: Then shall we all go together? It will be fun.

Sawat: Then let's go, everyone!

Sawat: It's a shame to face such problems, but I believe everyone will get through it.

Nittaya: Thank you all. I feel so grateful to have you by my side.

topic.scenario: At the host family's house in Preeng Village, Ba Subdistrict, Tha Tum District, Surin Province, on the morning of the ordination procession with elephants.
topic.situation_topic: Rooster-wattle divination ritual
topic.situation: After each host family carried their trays of offerings to worship the village's Phi Pakam Chang (the elephant guardian spirit), the village Brahmin shaman came to Somphon's house to perform the rooster-wattle divination ritual. This is an important ceremony that must be done after informing Phi Pakam Chang, according to the beliefs of the Preeng villagers. If the rooster's wattle is evenly curved and beautiful, it means that everything will proceed smoothly and bring good luck. But if the wattle is not attractive, it may indicate that things will not go smoothly or that bad luck may affect the ceremony. When they began the ritual and examined the chickens prepared for cooking, they found the wattles were unevenly curved, with several strange bends—not as beautiful as they should be. Thawi asked Somphon about it with concern.

But if the wattle is not beautiful, it may indicate misfortune or problems with the ceremony. When the ritual began and they examined the chicken prepared for cooking, they found the wattle was unevenly curved, with several strange bends — not as beautiful as it should be. Charoen asked Samran with concern.

topic.scenario: At the host's house in the Preeng village, Ba subdistrict, Tha Tum district, Surin province, on the morning of the procession when the ordination candidate was paraded on an elephant.
topic.situation_topic: Chicken wattle divination ceremony
topic.situation: After each host household had offered trays of sacrificial items to the Pa-kam elephant spirit, the village Brahmin priest came to Somphon’s house to perform the chicken wattle divination ceremony, an important ritual done after notifying the Pa-kam elephant spirit. According to the beliefs of the Preeng villagers, if the chicken’s wattle is evenly and attractively curved, it means everything will go smoothly and bring good luck. But if the wattle is not attractive, it could mean trouble or bad luck for the ceremony. When the ritual began and they took out the chicken prepared for cooking, they found the wattle was unevenly curved with strange bends at several points — not as it should be. Sombat asked Somphon about it with concern.

Samran: Yes, Wichian. I’ve never seen it before either. It’s very exciting.

Somphon: Is everyone ready? We need to go help organize the procession.

Sombat: I’m ready, Somphon, but I’m not sure what I should do.

Wichian: Don’t worry, Sombat. I’ll guide you.

Samran: Yes, let’s help each other so it gets done quickly.

Samran: Let’s go!

topic.scenario: At the large swing in the center of an Akha village in Chiang Rai Province, on the afternoon of the third day of the swing festival.
topic.situation_topic: The ritual of apologizing to the swing's guardian spirit and the swing rope by offering one pig.
topic.situation: During the day of the swing tradition, Sawat caused the village swing's rope to snap while trying to show off swinging to people in the village. According to custom this is a serious matter that requires one pig to be used in a ritual to apologize to the swing's guardian spirit so that no misfortune will befall anyone in the household. However, Sawat comes from a poor family and has no pigs left, so he is worried about debts he might have to incur from borrowing. While his friend Thawi is with him, Sawat asks what he should do.

part_1:
Thawi: Hello everyone. The weather is great today.

Sawat: Yes, Thawi, it really is. Perfect for swinging.

Udom: Hello you all. Where are you from?

Thawi: We're from Bangkok. We're here to join this year's swing festival.

Wichian: Welcome. This event is a lot of fun. Have you been here before?

Sawat: This is our first time, but we've heard this tradition has been around for a long time.

Udom: Yes, it's a tradition passed down for generations. The villagers are very proud.

Wichian: If you have any questions or want to know anything about the event, feel free to ask.

Thawi: Thank you very much, Wichian. I'd like to know why we swing at this event?

Udom: Swinging is a symbol of asking for blessings for happiness and prosperity.

Sawat: Sounds very interesting. Is there anything you recommend we try at the event?

Wichian: If you like local food, try khao lam (sticky rice in bamboo) and nam prik num (young chili paste). They're very delicious.

Thawi: Sounds tempting. Thanks for the recommendation.

Udom: You're welcome. Hope you enjoy the event.

Sawat: Definitely. Thanks a lot, Udom and Wichian, for the helpful information.

Wichian: My pleasure. If you need any help, just tell me.

Thawi: Thank you very much. You are very kind.
part_2:
Sawat: Sorry everyone, I have to quickly set up the room before the next meeting. See you later.

Wichian: I have to go buy a drink first. See you.

Thawi: Okay Sawat, Wichian, see you later.

Udom: Thawi, do you think Sawat will be okay? He looked stressed when talking about the swinging.

Thawi: I noticed too. He seems worried about violating the tradition.

Udom: Yes. Maybe he feels guilty for making a mistake.

Thawi: I think he just needs time to adjust. Talking with people at the event might help him feel better.

Udom: Agreed. Hearing the stories and meanings of the tradition might help him understand and relax.

Thawi: Yes. I'll try talking to him again after this in case he needs advice or encouragement.

Udom: Good. If he needs extra help, I'm willing to help too.

Thawi: Thank you very much, Udom. I'll tell him.

Udom: You're welcome. Hope he feels better soon.
part_3:
Wichian: I'm back. I went to buy drinks.

Thawi: Welcome back, Wichian. Did you get anything tasty?

Wichian: I got iced coffee. Very refreshing.

Udom: Nice. We're talking about apologizing to the swing's guardian spirit right now. Do you have any information?

Wichian: Oh yes. Apologizing to the swing's spirit is part of this tradition. We use one pig for the apology.

Thawi: Why use a pig?

Wichian: Pigs symbolize abundance and good luck. Using a pig in the apology is a way to show respect and ask for blessings for prosperity.

Udom: That sounds meaningful. Are there any special steps to be careful about?

Wichian: Mostly it's about preparing properly and following the correct procedures so the apology will be complete.

Thawi: Thanks a lot, Wichian, for the helpful information.

Wichian: You're welcome. But now I have to go grab a snack or a drink. See you later.

Udom: Okay Wichian, see you.

Thawi: Thanks again, Wichian. See you later.

Sawat: Hello everyone, I'm back.

Thawi: Welcome back, Sawat. How are you?

Sawat: I have something I want to consult about. I'm feeling very stressed right now.

Udom: What happened, Sawat?

Sawat: I broke the swing's rope while trying to show off swinging to people in the village.

Thawi: Wow, that's serious. How are you feeling now?

Sawat: I'm very worried because by tradition we must use one pig to apologize, but my family has no pigs left.

Udom: Don't worry, Sawat. We can find a way to apologize later.

Thawi: Yes, it's okay. We'll help think of a solution together.

Sawat: Thank you so much, everyone. I feel much better to have friends like you.

topic.situation: On the day of the swing festival, Nittaya caused the village's swing rope to break while trying to swing and show off to the villagers. topic.scenario: At the old wooden Thai house in Ban Tha Khae, Tha Khae subdistrict, Phatthalung province
topic.situation_topic: Gathering the descendants to perform the Nora dance for the ritual healer to treat Chan's illness
topic.situation: Chan became ill, which is believed to be punishment from the ritual healer because the descendants are not interested in continuing the Nora tradition. Chan asks for Nittaya, who by the rules must perform to receive the master and continue the lineage after returning from Bangkok: "That family's descendants must continue the Nora." But the truth is Nittaya is tied up with work in Bangkok and refuses to come back to participate in the ceremony.

topic.scenario: At an old wooden Thai house in Ban Tha Khae, Tha Khae Subdistrict, Phatthalung Province
topic.situation_topic: Gathering descendants to perform the Nora dance to honor the Kru-Moh and heal Wichian's illness
topic.situation: Wichian fell ill, which is believed to be due to punishment from the Kru-Moh because the descendants are not interested in carrying on the Nora tradition. Wichian asks for Somphon, who is supposed to perform the dance to receive the teacher and continue the lineage according to custom after returning from Bangkok: "A descendant of that family must continue the Nora." In reality, Somphon is tied up with work in Bangkok and refuses to return to join the ceremony.

topic.scenario: At Wat Lhai Hin Luang, Lhai Hin Subdistrict, Ko Kha District, Lampang Province
topic.situation_topic: Belief that ancestral spirits wait to receive merit
topic.situation: On the day when relatives must gather to make kway-salak, Charoen is waiting for Samran's younger sibling to come and write the dedication on the salak slip for their grandfather, because they believe that King Yama releases Grandfather's spirit today. If the descendants don't make merit for him, Grandfather will be sad and go hungry. Charoen asks Samran whether his sibling will arrive in time to write the dedication. In reality, Samran's sibling went on a trip with friends and doesn't intend to return.

part_1:
Samran: Grandma Charoen, the weather is really nice today at Wat Lhai Hin Luang.

Charoen: Yes, dear. In the past your grandfather and I used to come here often. It still feels as peaceful as ever.

Udom: I agree. The atmosphere here really helps me relax.

Narong: Yes. I also like coming here to make merit and rest my mind.

Samran: Grandma, what ceremonies will we do today?

Charoen: We'll start by offering sangkhatan (offerings to the monks), then we'll have group chanting.

Udom: Sounds great. I brought offerings. I hope we gain a lot of merit.

Narong: Me too. Coming to make merit together like this feels very good.

Samran: I'm glad to join the ceremony with everyone. Grandma, I'll help you carry the things.

Charoen: Thank you, my boy. Grandma is very proud of you.

Udom: Then let's begin the ceremony.

Narong: Yes, let's go so we don't waste time.

Samran: Let's go, everyone!
part_2:
Charoen: Oh dear, I forgot I have something to do. Sorry everyone, I have to go first.

Narong: I also have to buy coffee. See you again, everyone.

Samran: Okay, Grandma. Okay, Mr. Narong. See you.

Udom: We'll continue our conversation later.

Samran: Yes, Mr. Udom. I feel that if we don't honor the traditions your grandmother and grandfather practiced, she will be very upset.

Udom: Yes. Preserving the tradition is like honoring our ancestors.

Samran: I think so too. I don't want Grandfather's spirit to be left waiting.

Udom: Exactly. Coming together to make merit like this shows our love and respect for him.

Samran: Yes. I'll do my best to make Grandma proud.

Udom: Good job, Samran. Your grandmother will surely be proud of you.

Samran: Thank you, Mr. Udom. I'll do my best.

Udom: About ancestral spirits, right?

Samran: I feel the same. If we make merit for him, he will receive the merit and watch over us.

Narong: Yes. I've heard that if we don't make merit, he might be left waiting.

Udom: That's true. Keeping the tradition is a way of honoring him.

Samran: Okay, Mr. Narong.

Udom: See you soon.

Narong: Yes, I'll be back.

Udom: Yes, Grandma. Don't worry.

Charoen: Thank you, my grandchildren. I'm glad you are taking care of this.

Samran: It's nothing, Grandma. We all want Grandfather to receive merit.

Udom: Yes, Grandma. We'll do our best to make Grandfather happy.

Charoen: Thank you. I'm really proud of you all.

topic.scenario: At Wat Lai Hin Luang temple, Lai Hin subdistrict, Ko Kha district, Lampang province
topic.situation_topic: The belief that ancestral spirits wait to receive merit
topic.situation: On the day when relatives must gather to perform the kway salak ceremony, Prasoet is waiting for Sombun's younger sibling to come and write the dedication line for their grandfather, because they believe Lord Yama has released the grandfather's spirit today. If the descendants don't make merit for him, the grandfather will be sad and go hungry. Prasoet asks Sombun whether the younger sibling will arrive in time to write the dedication. In fact, Sombun's younger sibling went on a trip with friends and doesn't intend to come back.
topic.lie_objective: To spare the elder's feelings and give hope that the grandfather's spirit will receive merit
topic.leave_reason_B: I have a prior appointment I must hurry to take care of
topic.leave_reason_D_1: I need to go meet someone for a moment
topic.leave_reason_D_2: I need to help a coworker for a bit

Sombun: Grandma Prasoet, look, Wat Lai Hin Luang is so beautiful

Amphon: It's my first time here too. The atmosphere is wonderful

Samran: Yes, Amphon. I really like this place — it's very peaceful

Sombun: Grandma Prasoet, do you remember what was here back then?

Prasoet: I remember. Back then there was only the ordination hall and an old stupa, but now many new pavilions have been added

Amphon: And what ceremonies will we do today?

Samran: I heard we'll offer sangkathan (alms) and release birds and fish

Sombun: That's great. I like releasing birds and fish — it makes me feel good

Prasoet: Yes, making merit like this calms the mind and brings happiness

Amphon: I agree. Coming to the temple to make merit like this is very relaxing

Samran: Then let's get ready. The ceremony will start soon

Sombun: Let's go, Grandma Prasoet, Amphon, Samran

Samran: I also need to step out to meet someone for a moment. I'll be back

Sombun: Okay, Grandma Prasoet, Samran. See you

Amphon: Okay. So what should we do next, Sombun?

Sombun: I think we should talk about the tradition you told us about, Grandma Prasoet

Amphon: Yes, I think that's very important. If we don't respect our traditions, our grandparents will be sad

Sombun: Yes, I don't want Grandma Prasoet to feel bad or become ill because of this

Amphon: I agree. Preserving traditions brings our family closer together

Sombun: Yes, and it's a way to show respect to our ancestors

Amphon: So let's be sincere in our merit-making and continue the tradition

Sombun: Of course, Amphon. We'll do our best to make Grandma Prasoet proud

Amphon: Good. Let's prepare to make merit

Sombun: Let's go

Sombun: Welcome back, Samran. We were just talking about the tradition

Amphon: Yes, Samran. We were discussing the importance of preserving our customs

Samran: Good. I agree — keeping traditions makes us feel closer to our ancestors

Sombun: Samran, do you believe that ancestral spirits wait to receive merit?

Samran: I do. I think making merit for our ancestors shows respect and makes them happy

Sombun: Okay, Samran. See you

Amphon: Good luck, Samran. Come back soon

Samran: Thanks. See you all

Sombun wanted her grandchild to be strong, so she tried to pull Prani's hand and weave through the crowd to get closer to the medium to ask for blessings. Prani feared for her unborn child.

Sombun: Yes, Prani. Weather like this is perfect for coming to the shrine.

Prasit: Prani, you're so far along—can you still walk?

Prani: I can, P'Prasit, but I have to walk a little slowly.

Sawat: If you get tired, tell me, Prani. I'll help support you.

Prani: Thank you, P'Sawat.

Sombun: Prani, be careful, dear. You might slip and fall.

Prani: Yes, Mom. I'm being careful.

Prasit: P'Sawat, have you been here often?

Sawat: I have, but not very often. Mostly during festivals.

Prani: I really like the atmosphere here. It feels peaceful.

Sombun: That's right. This place is good for making wishes.

Prasit: What are you going to wish for, Prani?

Prani: I wish for the baby to be healthy and for an easy delivery.

Sawat: I hope your wish comes true, Prani.

Prani: Thank you, P'Sawat.

Sombun: Alright, let's go make offerings at the shrine.

Prasit: Let's go. It will get too late otherwise.

Sawat: Yes, let's go.

Sombun: I need to go to the restroom first. I'll be right back.

Sawat: I have to go take care of my child for a moment. I'll be right back.

Prani: Okay, Mom, P'Sawat.

Prasit: Prani, your mother seems very worried about you.

Prani: Yes. Mom is afraid I'll slip and that it will harm the baby.

Prasit: Your mother loves and worries about you a lot, Prani.

Prani: I know, but sometimes she overthinks things.

Prasit: I understand, but she just doesn't want anything to happen to you.

Prani: I know. I'll be as careful as possible.

Prasit: That's good. If you need anything, tell me.

Prani: Thank you, P'Prasit. I'm lucky to have people around who care.

Prasit: We all want you and the baby to be safe.

Prani: Yes. I'll take the best care of myself.

Sawat: I'm back. Sorry I was gone so long.

Prani: It's okay, P'Sawat. P'Prasit and I were just talking about Mom.

Prasit: That's right, P'Sawat. Have you heard about the rule forbidding pregnant women from watching the spirit medium?

Sawat: I've heard about it. They say pregnant women shouldn't get close to the procession.

Prani: Really? Why is it forbidden?

Sawat: They say it's a belief related to the safety of pregnant women.

Prasit: Yes. Sometimes it may be connected to energies or things like that.

Prani: Hmm... I never knew before.

Sawat: But it's just a belief, so don't worry too much.

Prani: Okay, thank you for telling me.

Sawat: You're welcome. But I have to go now—there's a work emergency I need to handle immediately.

Prani: Oh, I understand, P'Sawat.

Prasit: Good luck, P'Sawat.

Sawat: Thank you. See you again.

Prani: Okay, P'Sawat.

Sombun: I'm back, dear. Sorry I was gone so long.

Prani: It's okay, Mom.

Prasit: Mom, you came back in time to see the procession.

Sombun: Yes, Prani. Come closer so you can ask for blessings for your grandchild to be strong.

Prani: Mom, I think it's better if we stay right here.

Sombun: Why, dear? If we get closer you'll be able to make a clearer wish.

Prani: I've heard that pregnant women shouldn't get close to the procession.

Prasit: That's right, Mom. It's a belief that pregnant women should be careful about.

Sombun: But I want my grandchild to be safe and strong.

Prani: I understand, but I'm afraid the baby might be harmed.

Prasit: Mom, we can let her watch from here for Prani's safety.

Prani: Yes, Mom. Watching from here is enough.

Sombun: Hmm... okay. I understand.

Prani: Thank you, Mom.

Prasit: Thank you, Mom, for understanding.

Sombun: It's nothing. I'm just worried about my grandchild.

Prani: I know, Mom. Thank you for worrying about me.

Prasit: Dad, I think we should hold a small gathering here—invite friends to sit and talk.

Thawi: That's a good idea, child, but make sure to take care of the cleanliness.

Sombun: If you hold the event, I'll help cook. Is there any special dish you'd like?

Somphon: I'll go for sticky rice and grilled pork, P' Sombun. It will definitely be delicious.

Thawi: Sounds fun, but be careful about noise. Don't disturb the neighbors.

Prasit: Thank you all so much. I'm glad to have such a warm family.

Sombun: Yes. Our family will live together happily.

Somphon: Exactly. the family's happiness is the most important thing.
